inputs.original_text: This is how the system protects its own: the Punjab and Haryana High Court says pre-arrest bail can be revoked only with clear proof of misuse or changed circumstances, even though the stolen articles remain missing and the allegations are serious. Justice Sumeet Goel dismissed the cancellation plea, leaving the accused shielded while the public is told to produce proof that may be out of sight. Calling that a safeguard obscures what it does: turns strict rules into cover for keeping accountability just beyond reach.
inputs.modified_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has made the shield plain: pre-arrest bail can be revoked only with clear proof of misuse or changed circumstances. Yet the stolen articles are still missing and the allegations are serious, while Justice Sumeet Goel dismissed the cancellation plea. They call this a safeguard, but it looks more like a system designed to keep accountability out of reach—demanding proof that may be hidden while those already protected stay protected.
